text: Normal temperature is 38–39°C in adults and 39–40°C in calves; high temperature generally signals infection. Eyes: check for conjunctival infection (discharge), eye injury (often kept closed), and conjunctiva color — pale conjunctiva signals anemia, often seen with Liver Fluke. Mouth: examine the muzzle and mouth, especially with abnormal salivation, which can come from FMD lesions on the gum and tongue or from a foreign object like a piece of wood. Skin: check closely for external parasites like ticks, crusts (from mange or other irritation), and wounds.
